long_biography.plain_text:
Media entrepreneur Vladimir Gusinsky developed businesses that supplied programmes and finance to regional television stations as well as running national outlets. His holdings combined broadcasting with a daily newspaper and a weekly magazine produced in cooperation with Newsweek. He wanted to build a publishing institution whose name would outlast its founder.

His bank supported ballet and theatre, and he later encouraged other businesspeople to join his charitable giving. As president of the Russian Jewish Congress, he helped bring donors into an organisation funding schools, social services and cultural projects. Its grants and regional branches extended the undertaking beyond individual gifts.
